title: Monthly Order Count
description:
Count how many orders were placed in each **calendar month** (across all years). Return the year, month number, and order count.

**Table: orders**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| customer_id | INT |
| order_date | DATE |
| status | VARCHAR |
| total_amount | DECIMAL |

Output columns: `order_year`, `order_month`, `order_count`. Order by `order_year`, `order_month`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, order_date DATE, status VARCHAR, total_amount DECIMAL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,DATE '2026-01-05','completed',100.00),(2,2,DATE '2026-01-15','completed',75.50),(3,3,DATE '2026-02-07','pending',200.00),(4,4,DATE '2026-02-20','completed',150.00),(5,5,DATE '2026-02-28','completed',90.00),(6,1,DATE '2026-03-10','completed',60.00);
solution_sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) AS order_year, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) AS order_month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY order_year, order_month ORDER BY order_year, order_month
hints: EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) and EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) pull out the year and month.
GROUP BY both extracted values to get one row per year-month combination.
explanation: Extracting year and month and grouping by both creates one row per calendar month. January 2026 has 2 orders, February 3 orders, March 1 order.
